items.title: 67255_Helen Humes oral history interview
items.q: you made that album with Benny Carter, Shelly Manne, and Andre Previn, for Contemporary. And you enjoyed that, didn't you? I certainly did. That was one of the best sessions I ever had.

ctx.x: Yeah, he was with Benny, but he used alot of the Basie boys.

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I also wrote a little blues song for that picture. A thing called "No Good Man" that was sung in there by Helen Humes.

ctx.x: "Panic in the Streets" I did well, quite a lot of writing on that, arranging, and there was an interesting thing about "Panic in the Streets". That was the first picture ... no, oh no ... am I thinking about "Panic in the Streets?" No, I was thinking about "No Way Out". But "Panic in the Streets", yes, I also wrote a little blues song for that picture. A thing called "No Good Man" that was sung in there by Helen Humes. Yes, that was Jack Palance.
